name: Infrastructure as Code
description: All infrastructure changes must be made through code (Terraform, Pulumi, CDK) — no manual console changes.
content:
# Infrastructure as Code Rules

- All infrastructure must be defined in code — Terraform, Pulumi, AWS CDK, or equivalent IaC tool
- Never make manual changes in cloud consoles — if it's not in code, it doesn't exist and will be overwritten
- Use remote state storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob) with state locking — prevent concurrent modifications
- Use modules for reusable infrastructure patterns — VPC, database, load balancer modules shared across environments
- Parameterize environment differences — use variables for region, instance size, and scaling, not separate codebases
- Run `terraform plan` (or equivalent) in CI — review the diff before applying changes to production
- Require approval gates for production infrastructure changes — automated apply for staging, manual approval for production
- Tag all resources with environment, team, cost center, and project — enable cost tracking and ownership
- Use drift detection — alert when actual infrastructure diverges from the defined state
- Store secrets in a secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, Vault) — reference them in IaC, never hardcode
- Version your IaC modules — pin module versions and upgrade deliberately
- Document infrastructure architecture — maintain diagrams that reflect the current IaC state
